q: How does a Marmara electric arc furnace steel mill calculate its CBAM direct emissions?
title: EAF steel mill CBAM direct emissions
short: Use a carbon mass balance: carbon in electrodes, injected coal, charge carbon and alloys, plus natural gas burnt in burners and ladle heaters, minus carbon leaving in steel and slag. Divide by tonnes of billets or products. Scrap carried no embedded emissions under the transitional rules, and furnace electricity is not counted for steel.
audience: Scrap-based electric arc furnace mills in the Marmara and Kocaeli industrial corridor

ul: Graphite electrode consumption, from stock and purchase records.
Injected coal, anthracite or charge carbon, with carbon content from supplier analyses.
Natural gas for oxy-fuel burners, ladle preheating and reheating furnaces.
Lime and dolomite, if carbonate-based, and alloys that contain carbon.
Carbon in the steel produced and in slag, from your lab.

p: Scrap carried no embedded emissions under the transitional rules; check the definitive-period act. Bought pig iron, DRI or HBI and ferro-alloys covered by CBAM do. Add their tonnes times their verified embedded emissions, or the default values if the supplier gives none.

sections.h: Why EAF mills gain from actual values
p: Most of an EAF mill's full footprint is electricity, which is outside the CBAM figure for steel. Its direct figure is therefore far below a blast furnace mill's, but the EU default values for Turkey do not know that. Only verified actual data shows it.

example.title: Worked example: 100,000 t of billets in a year (illustrative inputs)
lines: Electrodes: 150 t x 3.664 t CO2 per t carbon = 549.6 t CO2
Injected coal: 1,500 t x 85% carbon x 3.664 = 4,671.6 t CO2
Burner and ladle gas: 2,000,000 scm x 2.05 kg CO2 per scm = 4,100 t CO2
Less carbon in steel: 100,000 t x 0.2% carbon x 3.664 = 732.8 t CO2
example.note: Quantities are illustrative. 3.664 is the CO2 to carbon mass ratio (44.01 / 12.011). Add precursors such as pig iron or DRI if you use them.
